title: Workflow for sprites?
author: Will_X_Intent
selftext:
I'm wondering what ya'lls workflow is for creating sprites and sprite animations.

Until recently, I was using ChatGPT Image 2.5 to generate pseudo pixel art, taking it to [https://pixel-refiner.app/](https://pixel-refiner.app/) or [https://retrodiffusion.ai/tools/pixel-art-fixer/](https://retrodiffusion.ai/tools/pixel-art-fixer/) to turn it into actual pixel art (have to use both, because sometimes one is better, and sometimes the other).  I would then take that image into Aseprite and fix some pixels.  Then I would point my AI at it, tell it to add it to the game, and also add it to the in game sprite inspector I had it make.

Animations...  are hard.  Sol/Astra likes to try to turn sprites into puppets to make animations.  They always look bad.  Image 2.5 can't get walking animations correct.  Over and over it make the legs have the same pose but moves the arms.   I heard making a video from your sprite then using frames from  the video to make an animation helps, but the video gen I used kept changing the sprite.  

Local gen has been a complete failure for me.  Slow, makes my computer loud af and then I cant use it for anything else.  And the output is so bad it cant be salvaged by hand.

comments.author: ZymzAlchemy
comments.body:
I find SOL 6.1 does a solid job if you provide it with an art style guide (this is the art style I want you to reproduce) and an asset list (this is a list of the assets I want, in the size/shape/spacing/grid formation and a detailed description of the asset (one block for each asset you want, sheets should be soec'd fully dimensions/spacing/cel layout accompanying the sprite/sheet you want created.

Provide it with your concept art, and tell if to execute the asset sheet against the style guide using the concept art as a visual identify reference.

YMMV. Be well, and keep creating.

replies.author: Will_X_Intent
replies.body: I did that too, with both Astra and Sol, gave it a large list of assets to create and the visual style (the visual style is well defined and documented, so I dont even need to prompt style).  It can do a decent job with individual sprites, though it's tastes are kinda basic.  They are like 80-90% as good as if I had generated the asset myself.  Making animation spritesheets for those items (like a potion bottle pouring) is still not great.

replies.author: ZymzAlchemy
replies.body:
When you say 'generated the asset by myself' do you mean prompting it in ChatGPT or something similar? If that's what you mean, give it the art guide along with something like 'use this as the canonical art style guide for this session do not deviate from the described style/aesthetic defined in the document' this can help with style/consistency in 'chat renders'. 

And as stupid as this might come across, you can make a 'sprite sheet template' of stick figures doing the thing you want and toss this at SOL telling it to use the sheet as a POSE REFERENCE ONLY and generate the describes sheet in the provided art style etc and so on.

comments.author: Evile_Gaming
comments.body:
Aat the moment, AI is pretty tragic at building Atlas/sprite sheets. It just cannot maintain consistancy and position very well, even the best models (... that's with just one sheet, it completely loses the plot when you have a character with dozens of animations).  I've spent more time trying to write a tool to get AI to generate usable atlas, than I have on the the game I'm making the sprites for.  
 I'm sure I'll get there eventually, but its a slog, unfortunately I think the training data for this is almost non-existent, the nature of the medium (highly complex layers images, with no annotations, held in private repos).  I never got any training for this kind of thing when I was working in the indusrty, I and my co-workers had to work it all out for ourselves.
